turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I used a **composition-similarity ranking**, prioritizing candidates close to high-zT training samples and checking nearby compositions for consistency. These are approximate predictions—not measured values or cross-validated model estimates.

| Rank | Candidate | Approximate zT | Evidence from the training data |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **c037** | **0.78** | Its Te = 0.50, Pb = 0.45 composition is almost identical to the training sample with Te = 0.50, Pb = 0.4525 and **zT = 0.782**. |
| 2 | **c010** | **0.71** | Sn = 0.55782 is extremely close to the Sn = 0.55556 training sample with **zT = 0.709**. This prediction has strong local support, though from only one very close example. |
| 3 | **c046** | **0.53** | Its Sn-rich Mg–Sn–Si composition lies near high-performing Mg-based samples: Sn-rich, Bi-doped examples reach **0.461–0.546**, while a Mg–Sn–Ge example reaches **0.664**. This requires more extrapolation than the first two selections. |
| 4 | **c043** | **0.50** | Closely resembles the Mg–Sb–Bi–Te training composition with **zT = 0.473**. A nearby Co-containing variant reaches **0.792**, providing additional—but less direct—support. |
| 5 | **c054** | **0.47** | Almost exactly matches the Mg–Sb–Bi–Te training sample with **zT = 0.473**, making this a well-supported local prediction. |

The first two choices have particularly close high-performing analogues. **Ranks 3–5 are less certain**, especially because small dopant changes can produce substantial target differences in this dataset. I did not generalize the isolated zT = 3.93 observation to chemically dissimilar candidates.

Final: c037, c010, c046, c043, c054
